subtitle: How a Lost Pension Became a Rebel Throne of Coin and Dust

panels.shot: epic dusk wide over the Ganges, with a half-lit treasury chest and a gleaming copper coin in the foreground
panels.action: Nana Sahib stands on the riverbank at Kanpur in rich Maratha garments beside Azimullah Khan in courtly attire, a heavy Company strongbox at their feet and a single paisa coin held up between finger and thumb against the burning sky.

dialogue.text: In June 1857, at Kanpur, a lost Maratha pension turned seized Company treasure into pay, courts and coins, as Nana Sahib and Azimullah Khan tried to buy rebel sovereignty before time ran out.

i18n.hi: जून 1857, कानपुर में खोई मराठा पेंशन ने ज़ब्त कंपनी ख़ज़ाने को बनाया बाग़ी तनख़्वाह, दरबार और सिक्कों की गद्दी—नाना साहब और अज़ीमुल्ला ख़ान बगावत की हुकूमत ख़रीदने निकले, समय हाथ से फिसलता रहा।

panels.shot: slow push-in from a grand durbar hall to an intimate corner where two men confer
panels.action: In the Bithur palace hall, portraits of Peshwas gaze down as Nana Sahib leans over a low table covered with British papers and ledgers, Azimullah Khan seated opposite with an ink-stained hand, both faces tense in lamplight.

dialogue.text: The story begins not with gunfire, but with paperwork: after Baji Rao II died in 1851, the Company pension that fed the Peshwa’s house stopped, and Nana Sahib’s claim was denied.

i18n.hi: कहानी शुरू होती है गोलियों से नहीं, कागज़ से: 1851 में बाजी राव द्वितीय के मरने पर पेशवा घराने की कंपनी पेंशन बंद हुई, और नाना साहब का दावा ठुकरा दिया गया।

panels.shot: close-up on Azimullah reading an English document, Nana watching
panels.action: Azimullah Khan, worldly and sharp, holds up a folded despatch stamped with the Company seal, while Nana Sahib stands behind him, fists tight, as the candlelight picks out the cold official lines.

dialogue.text: London petitions, court arguments, diplomatic journeys—Azimullah carried Nana’s case to distant desks. The answer that came back was firm: no extension, no inheritance, no Peshwa pension.

i18n.hi: लंदन अर्ज़ियाँ, अदालती बहसें, सियासी सफ़र—अज़ीमुल्ला नाना का मामला दूर–दराज़ दफ़्तरों तक ले गया। जवाब साफ़ था: न बढ़ोतरी, न विरासत, न पेशवा की पेंशन।

panels.shot: wide shot of Bithur estate with river and gardens, contrasted with a shadow over Nana
panels.action: From a veranda in Bithur, Nana Sahib looks over the Ganges and his dwindling estate, ledger books open beside him, as workers move slowly in the garden below under the rising summer heat.

dialogue.text: Without the pension, the Bithur estate shrank. Around Kanpur, tales of annexed Oudh and unpaid men spread. Money was vanishing from old courts, but flowing into Company treasuries and new cantonments.

i18n.hi: पेंशन के बिना बिठूर की जागीर सिमटती गई। कानपुर के इर्द–गिर्द अवध की छीनी रियासत और बे–तनख़्वाह लोगों की कहानियाँ फैलती रहीं। पुरानी अदालतों से रुपया गायब, कंपनी के ख़ज़ानों और नए छावनियों में भरता गया।

panels.shot: bird’s-eye over Kanpur cantonment and nearby Bithur, hinting at tension
panels.action: A high view shows the Kanpur cantonment with its parade ground and white barracks on one side, and on the other the clustered houses and temples of Bithur, the Ganges cutting between them like a pale ribbon.

dialogue.text: By early 1857, Kanpur stood as a key Company post on the Ganges. Beside it, Nana Sahib, the adopted son of a fallen Peshwa, watched a world ruled by ledgers and artillery, not hereditary claims.

i18n.hi: 1857 की शुरुआत तक कानपुर गंगा किनारे कंपनी का बड़ा ठिकाना था। बगल में गिरा हुआ पेशवा का दत्तक बेटा नाना साहब, खाते–किताब और तोपों से चलती दुनिया को देख रहा था, वंश–दावे की नहीं।

panels.shot: crowded courtyard mid-shot, sepoys gathered around Nana
panels.action: In a dusty Kanpur courtyard, sepoys with bayonets slung stand in a tense ring around Nana Sahib, who addresses them from a raised platform, while Azimullah waits at his side with a palm-leaf notebook.

dialogue.speaker: nana_sahib_and_azimullah_khan
dialogue.text: Stay here. Fight here. Your pay will be doubled.

i18n.hi: यहीं रहो। यहीं लड़ो। तुम्हारी तनख़्वाह दुगनी होगी।

panels.shot: dramatic interior of Company treasury mid-action freeze
panels.action: Inside the Kanpur treasury, massive chests are being prised open by rebel guards as Nana Sahib stands at the threshold, back straight, and Azimullah counts heaps of coins and stacks of papers on the floor.

dialogue.text: When Kanpur rose in June, Nana seized the Company magazine and treasury. To hold sepoys who might march to Delhi, he promised double pay—and turned captured funds into rebel wages.

i18n.hi: जून में कानपुर में बगावत उठी तो नाना ने कंपनी का दारू–गोदाम और ख़ज़ाना कब्ज़ा लिया। दिल्ली की ओर निकलते सिपाहियों को रोकने के लिए उसने दुगनी तनख़्वाह का वादा किया—और ज़ब्त रुपये को बाग़ी मज़दूरी बना दिया।

panels.shot: close-up of coins being sorted, Azimullah’s hands moving fast
panels.action: A tight shot shows Azimullah Khan’s fingers moving through piles of rupees and copper coins on a low table, marking tallies in a ledger, while Nana’s hand enters the frame to point at a growing column of figures.

dialogue.text: Azimullah became collector and administrator. The seized money had to stretch across thousands of men, rations, horse fodder and powder. Every extra rupee of promise meant a risk of collapse.

i18n.hi: अज़ीमुल्ला वसूलीदार और काम–काज का मालिक बना। छीना हुआ पैसा हज़ारों सिपाहियों, राशन, घोड़ों के चारे और बारूद पर फैलना था। हर extra रुपये का वादा, ढह जाने का नया ख़तरा था।

panels.shot: low-angle interior of an improvised court, Nana presiding
panels.action: Under an awning near the river, Nana Sahib sits on a raised seat like a Maratha prince, Azimullah at his side with papers, while petitioners—soldiers and townsmen—stand in rows before them in the hot glare.

dialogue.text: With the British shut inside their entrenchment, Nana held durbars. Pay disputes, supplies, local grievances—soldiers and civilians now came to his camp court. Money became the thread binding this newborn authority.

i18n.hi: अंग्रेज़ अपने घेराबंदी में क़ैद थे, तो नाना ने दरबार लगाए। तनख़्वाह के झगड़े, रसद, देसी शिकायतें—सिपाही और कस्बे वाले अब उसके डेरा–दरबार में आते। पैसा, इस नई हुकूमत को बाँधने वाली डोरी बन गया।

panels.shot: intimate workshop shot, focus on coin dies and hammer
panels.action: In a dim corner room, a native engraver kneels before a simple anvil as Azimullah watches, and Nana Sahib stands behind them, overseeing the striking of fresh copper coins from rough dies laid out on cloth.

dialogue.text: Then came a sovereign act: new copper paisa coins were ordered. Struck in the name of Nana Sahib, they declared, in metal, a rebel state that claimed the Peshwa’s mantle on the banks of the Ganges.

i18n.hi: फिर आई हुकूमत की चाल: नए तांबे के पैसे ढलने का हुक्म हुआ। नाना साहब के नाम पर ढले ये सिक्के, गंगा किनारे पेशवा की चादर ओढ़े एक बाग़ी रियासत को धातु में ऐलान कर रहे थे।

panels.shot: macro close-up of a freshly struck paisa glinting, fingers holding it
panels.action: A single freshly struck paisa coin lies in Azimullah’s palm as Nana Sahib lifts it to the light, its crude yet distinct design catching the glint of the sun through a small lattice window.

dialogue.speaker: nana_sahib_and_azimullah_khan
dialogue.text: This is not their coin. This is ours.

i18n.hi: ये उनका सिक्का नहीं। ये हमारा है।

panels.shot: street-level shot as a market transaction occurs using the new coin
panels.action: In a Kanpur bazaar lane, a sepoy hands a gleaming copper coin to a grain seller, who hesitates, looks toward a distant rebel guard, then slowly weighs the coin in his hand before scooping chaff-lined wheat into a bag.

dialogue.text: Thomson’s account and surviving coins show a brief reality: rebel money circulated in Kanpur’s markets, paying for wheat and work, even as traders weighed its worth under the shadow of cannon smoke.

i18n.hi: थॉमसन की रपट और बचे हुए सिक्के दिखाते हैं एक छोटी–सी हक़ीकत: बाग़ी पैसा कानपुर की मंडियों में घूम रहा था, गेहूँ और मज़दूरी का हिसाब चुकाता, जबकि सौदागर उसकी क़ीमत तोप के धुएँ की छाया में तौल रहे थे।

panels.shot: overhead shot of ledger pages revealing shrinking balances
panels.action: A bird’s-eye view of an open ledger on a table shows lines of expenditure racing ahead of receipts, while Nana Sahib and Azimullah stand on either side, their silhouettes dark, as summer dust drifts over the ink.

dialogue.text: But the treasury was finite. Without regular land revenue like the Company’s, each day’s double pay and rations ate into the captured hoard. Rebel finances were a candle burning hard at both ends.

i18n.hi: पर ख़ज़ाना सीमित था। कंपनी की तरह तय ज़मीनी लगान के बिना, रोज़ की दुगनी तनख़्वाह और राशन उस पकड़ी गई दौलत को खा रहे थे। बाग़ी माली व्यवस्था दो सिरों से जलती मोमबत्ती बन गई।

panels.shot: medium shot in camp as restless sepoys argue over arrears
panels.action: In the rebel camp outside Kanpur, a knot of sepoys argue and gesture toward the entrenchment, while Azimullah tries to calm them, and Nana stands slightly apart, listening, jaw set, as dusk gathers.

dialogue.text: As the siege dragged on, trust frayed. Promised pay was delayed or disputed, some men wanted to move on, others doubted the staying power of Nana’s rule. Money had started the bond; its shortage strained it.

i18n.hi: घेराबंदी लंबी चली तो भरोसा उधड़ने लगा। वादा की तनख़्वाह देर से आई या झगड़े में फँसी, कुछ लोग आगे बढ़ना चाहते थे, कुछ नाना की सल्तनत की उम्र पर ही शक करने लगे। पैसा ने रिश्ता बनाया था; अब उसकी कमी उसे तोड़ रही थी।

panels.shot: wide shot of Kanpur after British reoccupation, treasury and streets quiet
panels.action: A later view of Kanpur shows British troops marching past the once-seized treasury building, its doors now guarded by redcoats, as the bazaar lies subdued and the Ganges flows indifferent in the background.

dialogue.text: When Kanpur fell back into British hands, Nana and Azimullah disappeared from the town. Their experiment in rebel finance ended abruptly, leaving coins, accounts and memories rather than a lasting state.

i18n.hi: कानपुर फिर अंग्रेज़ी क़ब्ज़े में आया तो नाना और अज़ीमुल्ला town से ओझल हो गए। बाग़ी माली तजुर्बा अचानक थम गया, पीछे रह गए सिर्फ़ सिक्के, हिसाब–किताब और यादें—कोई टिकाऊ रियासत नहीं।

panels.shot: museum-style close-up of preserved Nana Sahib coins under soft light
panels.action: Under soft museum lighting, a handful of preserved Nana Sahib paisa coins rest on dark velvet, their worn surfaces and legends visible, while a faint reflection hints at a viewer studying them in silence.

dialogue.text: Today, in collections far from Kanpur, Nana Sahib’s paisas survive as small copper witnesses. They show that in 1857, power was claimed not only with rifles, but with stamped metal and the promise of pay.

i18n.hi: आज, कानपुर से दूर–दराज़ संग्रहों में, नाना साहब के पैसे तांबे के छोटे गवाह बनकर बचे हैं। वे बताते हैं कि 1857 में ताकत सिर्फ़ बंदूक से नहीं, मुहर लगे धातु और तनख़्वाह के वादे से भी माँगी गई थी।

panels.shot: final contemplative wide over the Ganges at Bithur, empty palace balcony
panels.action: At Bithur, the empty palace balcony overlooks the slow Ganges at sunset, invisible voices of history in the air where Nana Sahib and Azimullah once planned, the river carrying the light away.

dialogue.text: Nana Sahib’s rebel treasury rose on lost pension and captured coin, but could not last without steady revenue or deep trust. His brief coinage reminds us that sovereignty is minted in money—and in belief.

i18n.hi: नाना साहब का बाग़ी ख़ज़ाना खोई पेंशन और पकड़े सिक्कों पर उठा, पर बिना पक्की आमदनी और गहरे भरोसे के टिक न सका। उसके थोड़े–से सिक्के याद दिलाते हैं कि हुकूमत रुपये में ढलती है—और यक़ीन में भी।

subtitle_i18n.en: How a Lost Pension Became a Rebel Throne of Coin and Dust
subtitle_i18n.hi: कैसे छीनी गई पेंशन बनी बाग़ी तख़्त–सिक्का और धूल
